courses.title: HTML & CSS Foundations
courses.desc: Create semantic, accessible and responsive websites from the first HTML document to polished layouts.

lessons.t: How the web works and HTML document structure
lessons.body:
A browser requests a resource from a server, receives HTML, CSS, JavaScript and media, then builds and displays the page. HTML provides meaning and structure rather than visual styling. A standard document uses a doctype declaration, an html root, a head for metadata and a body for visible content.
Example: place the page title in the head and the main heading inside the body. Use one clear h1 for the page's primary topic.

Semantic elements describe the purpose of content. Use header, nav, main, section, article, aside and footer to make page regions understandable. Headings should follow a logical hierarchy, while paragraphs, lists, blockquotes and emphasis communicate text structure.
Avoid choosing elements only because of their default appearance. Semantic markup improves maintainability, accessibility and the ability of assistive technology to navigate a page.

Use anchors for navigation and buttons for actions. Images need useful alternative text when they convey information; decorative images can use empty alt text. Tables are for tabular data and should have header cells. Forms collect user input through labels, inputs, selects, textareas and submit buttons.
Associate each label with its control, choose appropriate input types and provide clear validation messages.

lessons.t: CSS selectors, cascade and box model
lessons.body:
CSS rules contain a selector and declarations. Selectors target elements by type, class, id, attributes or relationships. The cascade resolves competing rules using origin, importance, specificity and source order. Every element is laid out using the box model: content, padding, border and margin.
Use box-sizing: border-box for predictable sizing. Prefer reusable classes over repeated inline styles.

Flexbox is useful for one-dimensional alignment in a row or column. Grid is useful for two-dimensional layouts with rows and columns. Responsive design adapts to available space using flexible units, max-width, wrapping and media queries.
Start with a small-screen layout, then add breakpoints only when the content needs them. Test navigation, forms and cards at narrow and wide viewport widths.

Accessible pages provide keyboard operation, visible focus, sufficient contrast, descriptive link text and meaningful labels. Validate HTML, inspect browser developer tools and check network and console errors. Optimize image dimensions and avoid unnecessary assets before publishing.
A final review should include keyboard-only navigation, zoom, mobile layout, broken links and form behavior.

quiz.q: Which element represents the primary content of a page?
Which attribute supplies alternative text for an image?
Which element is intended for site navigation links?
Which CSS property controls space inside an element's border?
Which layout system is designed for two-dimensional rows and columns?
What does a media query help a stylesheet do?
o: Adapt styles to device or viewport conditions

quiz.q: Which control should normally trigger an action rather than navigate to a URL?
What is the purpose of a form label?
Which practice improves keyboard accessibility?
What should be checked before publishing a website?
o: Keyboard use, mobile layout and broken links

courses.title: JavaScript Basics
courses.desc: Understand modern JavaScript and use it to build interactive browser experiences.

lessons.body:
JavaScript runs in browsers and other runtimes. In a browser it can respond to events, update the DOM and communicate with APIs. Load scripts with defer when they depend on parsed HTML, and use modules to organize larger applications.
Open the browser console to inspect output and errors. Keep presentation in CSS, structure in HTML and behavior in JavaScript where practical.

Use const when a binding should not be reassigned and let when reassignment is required. Common values include strings, numbers, booleans, null, undefined, arrays and objects. Operators perform arithmetic, comparisons, logical tests and assignments.
Use strict equality (===) to avoid unexpected type coercion. Convert user input deliberately because form values are commonly strings.

if, else if and else select a path based on a condition. for, while and for...of repeat work. Arrays store ordered collections and provide methods such as map, filter, find, includes and reduce.
Choose the method that expresses the intention clearly. Avoid changing an array while iterating over it unless the behavior is deliberate.

Functions package reusable behavior. Parameters receive input and return sends a result to the caller. Arrow functions provide concise syntax, while closures allow a function to retain access to its surrounding scope.
Use try/catch around operations that can fail, and show helpful messages instead of silently swallowing errors. Keep functions focused and name them by the action they perform.

Objects group related properties and methods. The Document Object Model represents the page as nodes that JavaScript can query and update. Use querySelector, createElement, textContent and classList for common tasks.
Register event listeners for clicks, form submissions and keyboard actions. Prefer textContent for user-provided text to avoid interpreting it as HTML.

Promises represent work that completes later. async and await make promise-based code easier to read. fetch sends HTTP requests; check response.ok, parse the response and handle network errors.
Show loading, success and error states in the interface. Do not assume a request succeeded merely because fetch returned a response.

quiz.q: Which keyword declares a binding that cannot be reassigned?
Which operator checks strict equality?
Which array method creates a new array by transforming each item?
What does a function's return statement do?
o: Sends a result back to the caller

quiz.q: Which API is commonly used to select the first matching DOM element?
Which property is safer for inserting plain user text into an element?
What does addEventListener register?
What does await do inside an async function?
o: Waits for a promise to settle before continuing
Converts a string to a number

quiz.q: Which fetch check helps detect an HTTP error response?
Why should asynchronous code handle errors?
o: Network and server operations can fail

courses.title: UI/UX Design Essentials
courses.desc: Plan, prototype and evaluate useful digital experiences through user-centered design.

lessons.body:
User experience covers the complete experience of using a product, including usefulness, usability and satisfaction. User interface design focuses on the controls and visual surfaces people interact with. User-centered design begins with user needs rather than personal assumptions.
Define the audience, their goals, context and pain points before choosing a visual style.

Research methods include interviews, observation, surveys and analysis of existing behavior. A persona summarizes a meaningful user group; it should be grounded in evidence rather than stereotypes. A journey map shows stages, actions, questions and friction points.
Turn findings into clear problem statements and prioritize issues by user impact and frequency.

Information architecture organizes content so people can find it. Navigation labels should be familiar and consistent. Wireframes show hierarchy, content placement and key interactions without requiring finished visual styling.
Create low-fidelity sketches first, then refine the information flow. Test whether users can complete important tasks without being coached.

Visual hierarchy guides attention through size, weight, spacing, alignment and contrast. Typography should be readable at common screen sizes and use a limited, consistent type scale. Colour communicates meaning but should not be the only way to convey status.
Check text contrast and maintain consistent spacing and component styles across screens.

Interaction design defines how controls respond to user actions. Provide feedback for loading, success, errors, disabled states and destructive actions. Prototypes can range from clickable wireframes to high-fidelity simulations.
Prototype the highest-risk task flows first. Make controls predictable and ensure users can recover from mistakes.

Usability testing asks representative users to complete realistic tasks while the team observes where they struggle. Use neutral prompts, record task completion and identify recurring friction. Iterate based on evidence.
A handoff should include component states, spacing, typography, responsive behavior, assets and accessibility notes.

quiz.q: What is the main focus of user-centered design?
Which research method involves observing users performing tasks?
What does a persona summarize?
What is a wireframe primarily used to communicate?
Which principle helps users notice the most important content first?
Why should colour not be the only way to show an error?
o: Some users may not distinguish the colour

quiz.q: What is a prototype useful for?
o: Testing an interaction before full implementation

quiz.q: Which is a good usability test prompt?
o: Show me how you would find the course
The answer is in the menu

quiz.q: What should usability testing prioritize?
o: Observed user difficulties and task outcomes

quiz.q: What belongs in a useful design handoff?

courses.title: Full-Stack Web Development
courses.desc: Connect frontend interfaces, backend services, databases, authentication and deployment into a complete application.

lessons.body:
A full-stack application typically has a client, server/API and persistent data store. HTTP requests carry methods, paths, headers and optional bodies. GET retrieves data, POST creates or triggers processing, PUT/PATCH updates and DELETE removes resources.
Separate responsibilities so the browser handles presentation while the server validates business rules and protects data.

A component represents a reusable part of the interface. State stores values that can change, while props or parameters pass data into components. Keep UI state close to where it is used and derive values instead of duplicating them.
Design loading, empty, error and success states. Validate forms on the client for usability and again on the server for security.

An API defines how clients interact with server capabilities. Use clear resource-oriented routes, consistent status codes and predictable JSON responses. Validate required fields, types, lengths and allowed values before processing.
Return useful error messages without exposing stack traces, secrets or internal implementation details.

Relational databases store information in tables connected by primary and foreign keys. Normalize repeated data where appropriate and define constraints to protect integrity. CRUD operations create, read, update and delete records.
Use parameterized queries or a safe ORM, indexes for common lookup patterns and transactions when multiple changes must succeed together.

Authentication establishes who a user is; authorization determines what that user may do. Store password hashes rather than plaintext passwords, use secure session or token handling and restrict administrative operations on the server.
Apply least privilege, validate input, protect secrets with environment variables and use HTTPS in production. Never rely only on hiding a button in the frontend.

Unit tests check small functions, integration tests check connected modules and end-to-end tests exercise user journeys. Configure environment-specific settings and build reproducible deployment steps.
Monitor logs and errors, back up important data and keep dependencies updated. A successful deployment is not complete until core flows are verified in production.

quiz.q: Which HTTP method is commonly used to retrieve a resource?
What is the role of a frontend component?
Where should important business-rule validation occur?
What does a primary key identify?
o: A unique row in a table

quiz.q: What is authentication?
What is authorization?
o: Deciding what an authenticated user may access

quiz.q: How should passwords be stored?
Why use parameterized database queries?
What does an integration test examine?
Where should production secrets be stored?

courses.title: Data Science with Python
courses.desc: Use Python to prepare, explore, analyze and communicate evidence from structured datasets.

lessons.t: Data science workflow and Python environment
lessons.body:
A data science project begins with a question and an understanding of the available data. A typical workflow includes acquisition, cleaning, exploration, analysis or modeling, evaluation and communication.
Use a virtual environment to isolate dependencies and notebooks for exploratory work. Record assumptions and keep a reproducible copy of the data preparation steps.

Python provides the language foundation, while NumPy supports efficient numerical arrays. Pandas provides Series and DataFrame structures for tabular data. Read data from CSV or other supported formats and inspect shape, columns and data types.
Use head, info and describe to understand a dataset before making conclusions.

Check for missing values, duplicates, inconsistent categories, invalid ranges and incorrect data types. Decide whether to remove, replace or preserve missing values based on the context and the analysis question.
Convert dates and numeric fields carefully. Keep a record of transformations so the work can be repeated and audited.

Exploratory data analysis uses summaries and charts to understand distributions, relationships, outliers and possible data quality problems. Histograms show distributions, box plots summarize spread and scatter plots reveal relationships between two numeric variables.
Choose chart types that match the question, label axes and avoid implying causation from correlation.

Descriptive statistics summarize a sample; inferential methods help reason about a wider population under assumptions. Machine learning uses data to learn patterns for prediction or grouping. Split data into training and test sets before evaluating a model.
Choose metrics that match the task. Accuracy alone can be misleading when classes are imbalanced.

A strong report connects the original question, method, evidence, limitations and practical recommendation. Explain uncertainty and avoid claims that the data cannot support. Protect personal information and consider bias in collection and modeling.
Use clear visuals and plain language so stakeholders can understand what the analysis does and does not show.

quiz.q: Which Python library is commonly used for tabular data analysis?
What does a DataFrame represent in Pandas?
Which step should usually happen before modeling?
What does df.info() help inspect?
o: Column data types and non-null counts

quiz.q: Which chart is useful for viewing a numeric distribution?
What is an outlier?
o: An observation unusually distant from others

quiz.q: Why split data into training and test sets?
o: To evaluate performance on held-out data
To increase the number of labels

quiz.q: What does correlation indicate?
o: Proof that one variable causes another

quiz.q: Why can accuracy be misleading on imbalanced data?
o: A majority-class model may score highly while missing the minority class

quiz.q: What should a responsible analysis report include?

courses.title: Digital Marketing Mastery
courses.desc: Plan measurable campaigns using audience research, content, search, social channels and analytics.

lessons.body:
Digital marketing uses online channels to reach and engage audiences. Begin with a business objective such as awareness, leads or sales, then define a measurable outcome. A strategy connects audience needs, positioning, message, channels and budget.
Use SMART objectives: specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound. Avoid choosing channels before understanding the audience.

Research audience needs, questions, motivations and barriers using interviews, analytics and search behavior. Segment audiences by relevant needs or behaviors rather than assumptions. The customer journey may include awareness, consideration, conversion and retention.
Match content and calls to action to the stage a person is in. Keep messaging consistent while adapting the format to each channel.

Content marketing creates useful material that attracts and helps an audience, such as articles, videos, guides and case studies. A content calendar plans topics, formats, owners and publishing dates. Social media requires platform-appropriate creative and genuine interaction.
Prioritize usefulness and consistency over posting frequency alone. Include accessible captions and clear calls to action.

Search engine optimization improves how useful pages can be discovered in organic search. Research search intent, write descriptive titles, organize headings, improve page speed and create helpful content. Paid search uses bids and ad relevance to show sponsored listings.
Do not stuff keywords. Align landing pages with the promise made in the search result or advertisement.

Email campaigns use permission-based lists, relevant segmentation and clear messages. Subject lines should set accurate expectations. Landing pages should explain the offer, reduce friction and provide a clear next step.
Measure delivery, clicks and conversions while respecting consent and unsubscribe requirements. Test one meaningful change at a time when possible.

Analytics helps evaluate whether activity contributes to the objective. Common measures include reach, impressions, click-through rate, conversion rate and cost per acquisition. Define each metric and its measurement window before comparing campaigns.
Use tagged campaign links and consistent reporting. Treat results as evidence for the next experiment, not as proof of causation without a suitable test.

quiz.q: What should guide the choice of campaign channels?
What does a SMART objective include?
Which stage usually comes before consideration in a customer journey?
What is content marketing intended to provide?
o: Useful material for a defined audience

quiz.q: What does SEO primarily aim to improve?
What is a landing page?
o: A page focused on a specific campaign action

quiz.q: Which email practice is appropriate?
o: Use permission-based lists and honor unsubscribe requests

quiz.q: What does conversion rate measure?
o: The share of visitors completing a desired action

quiz.q: What is a KPI?
o: A metric linked to an objective

quiz.q: Why use tagged campaign links?
o: To attribute traffic to a campaign source

courses.title: Python Programming for Beginners
courses.desc: Learn Python syntax, problem solving, data structures, functions and file handling through practical examples.

lessons.t: Installing Python and writing your first program
lessons.body:
Python is a general-purpose language known for readable syntax. Install a supported version, confirm it is available from the terminal and use an editor or interactive shell to run code. The print function displays output and comments explain intent.
A Python script executes statements in order unless control flow changes that order. Save files with the .py extension and run them from the correct working directory.

Variables are names that refer to values. Common built-in types include int, float, str and bool. input reads text from the user, so convert it when numeric calculations are needed. f-strings format values clearly.
Choose meaningful names and validate input before using it. Understand the difference between assignment and comparison.

Arithmetic operators perform calculations, comparison operators produce Boolean results and logical operators combine conditions. if, elif and else select which block runs. Indentation defines Python code blocks.
Break complex conditions into smaller named checks. Test boundary values such as zero, negative numbers and empty strings.

for loops iterate over sequences and while loops repeat while a condition remains true. Lists are ordered and mutable, tuples are ordered and immutable, sets store unique values and dictionaries map keys to values.
Use range for numeric sequences and choose a collection based on the operations the program needs.

Functions make code reusable and easier to test. Parameters accept input and return provides output. Modules organize related functions and can be imported into another script. Exceptions represent runtime problems that can be handled with try and except.
Keep functions focused, avoid unnecessary global variables and catch specific exceptions when possible.

Use with open(...) to read or write files safely; specify an encoding for text. Debug by reproducing a problem, reading the traceback and checking variable values near the failure. Test normal, boundary and invalid inputs.
Practice by building a calculator, number guessing game, contact list or simple expense tracker. Divide each project into small functions.

courses.title: Graphic Design Fundamentals
courses.desc: Build strong visual compositions with typography, colour, layout, imagery and production-ready exports.

lessons.body:
Graphic design communicates a message through visual elements. Core principles include contrast, alignment, repetition, proximity, balance and hierarchy. A design brief identifies the audience, purpose, message, format and constraints.
Start with the communication goal. Every decorative choice should support clarity rather than compete with the message.

Composition arranges elements within a defined space. Grids provide consistent alignment, while whitespace separates groups and improves scanning. Balance can be symmetrical or asymmetrical depending on the intended energy and emphasis.
Use consistent margins and spacing rules. Check the design at its actual display size, not only while zoomed in.

Typography affects tone, hierarchy and readability. Consider typeface category, weight, size, line height, line length and letter spacing. A clear hierarchy distinguishes titles, section headings, body text and captions.
Limit the number of type families and use weights intentionally. Ensure body text remains readable on small screens and in print.

Colour relationships can create harmony, contrast and emphasis. Hue, saturation and value describe different aspects of colour. Build a palette with primary, secondary and neutral roles, then test combinations for sufficient contrast.
Never rely on colour alone to communicate meaning. Check how the design works for viewers with different colour-vision abilities.

Choose imagery that supports the message and has suitable resolution and usage rights. Icons should share a consistent visual style and remain understandable at their display size. Brand systems define repeatable choices such as logo use, colour, typography and imagery.
Avoid stretching raster images. Keep source assets organized and use vector formats for artwork that needs to scale cleanly.

Prepare files for their intended output. Print work may require bleed, correct colour settings and sufficient resolution; digital work needs optimized dimensions and suitable formats. Keep editable source files and export clearly named deliverables.
Review spelling, alignment, contrast, image quality and licensing. Present the final work with a short explanation of the design problem and decisions.

What does a grid help a designer maintain?
What is visual hierarchy?
o: An arrangement that guides attention by importance

quiz.q: Which typography choice usually improves body readability?

quiz.q: What do hue, saturation and value describe?
